title: Explicit expression and fast algorithms for the inverse of some matrices arising from implicit time integration

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (2.9), definition of the generalized binomial coefficient at i=0
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (2.8), extended to i=0, gives B(c_n,c_0)=prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(c_n-c_k)/prod_{k=1}^{n}(c_k-c_0), because (-1)^n prod_{k!=0}(c_0-c_k)=prod_{k=1}^{n}(c_k-c_0). But (2.9) inserts an additional factor (-1)^n. Thus (2.9) disagrees with (2.8). For equidistant nodes, (2.9) gives (-1)^n whereas the subsequent corollary requires the ordinary binomial coefficient binom(n,0)=1. Consequently the second form of Theorem 2.2 is wrong whenever i=0 or j=0 if (2.9) is used.

For i != j, evaluating psi'(x)=sum_{m!=i} prod_{k!=i,m}(x-c_k) at x=c_j leaves only the m=j term, namely prod_{k!=i,j}(c_j-c_k). The displayed lemma instead gives prod_{k!=j}(c_j-c_k), which has an extra factor c_j-c_i and is therefore incorrect. The later prose derivation itself gives the correct prod_{k!=i,j} expression, leaving contradictory versions of the claimed lemma in the paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (2.18) and the proof of Theorem 2.4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The asserted identity H^T = F [[0,c_0^T],[c_0,C_n]] is false. From H_{i,i-1}=i (with zero-based indices), H^T has superdiagonal entries 1,2,...,n, so the required factorization is H^T=F diag(0,D_n), not a factorization involving C_n=diag(c_1,...,c_n). The next displayed calculation silently replaces C_n by D_n, which does not follow from (2.18). Thus the stated proof of Theorem 2.4 is invalid as written, even though a corrected factorization can lead to the intended result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction versus the BIM discussion immediately after Theorem 2.4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction says that for c_i=i the inverse BIM matrix is exactly W_n^T. Later the paper says that the inverse BIM matrix is N = D_n(V_n D_n V_n^{-1}D_n^{-1})D_n^{-1}+D_n^{-1}. These expressions are not generally equal: for c_i=i, Theorem 2.4 gives W_n^T=V_nD_nV_n^{-1}D_n^{-1}, whereas the later N includes extra left/right D_n factors and an added D_n^{-1}. Already for n=1, W_n^T=1 but the displayed N equals 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Example 3 and the stated prerequisites of Algorithms 3.1–3.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algorithms are explicitly stated for c(0)<c(1)<...<c(n), and the claimed improved behavior of (3.10) also assumes c_0<c_1<...<c_n. Example 3 instead defines c_i=1/2+1/2 cos((2i+1)pi/(2n+1)), which is strictly decreasing in i: c_0>c_1>...>c_n=0. The experiments claim to apply Algorithms 3.2 and 3.3 to Examples 1–4 without stating any reordering, so Example 3 violates the algorithms' declared input condition.

The claimed 'Chebyshev nodes in (0,1)' are not standard Chebyshev roots or Lobatto nodes. With i=n, the stated formula has angle pi and hence c_n=0, contradicting the asserted interval (0,1). Standard n+1 Chebyshev roots would use denominator 2(n+1), while Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes use a different index/denominator convention. Thus the experiment is mislabeled and its node specification contradicts its stated domain.

The study defines errors by treating a quadruple-precision result W^q as 'exact.' Quadruple precision is not an exact reference, particularly for products/recurrences involving up to 10,000 nodes and for the cancellation-prone diagonal sums that the paper itself identifies. Therefore Err_1 and Err_2 are merely long-double-versus-quadruple discrepancies, not validated numerical errors. A higher-precision/arbitrary-precision reference, a residual/backward-error analysis, or both are required before claims of accuracy can be made.

The supplied reference list contains only entries [23]–[27], while the text repeatedly cites [1] through [22], including substantive attributions such as '[2]' for Corollary 2.3, '[11]' for the Runge–Kutta system, and '[17]' for BIM. These citations are unresolved in the paper as provided, preventing verification of attribution and prior-work claims.

The proof invokes equations '(2.11)' and '(2.12)' twice ('It follows from ... (2.11) and Lemma 2.1' and 'Combining ... (2.12)'), but neither numbered equation is present in the supplied Section 2. The actual immediately preceding displayed identities are (2.6) and (2.7). As written, the proof has broken references at the steps needed to derive the theorem.
